D.t: Charles Booker trails by 13.9 and wins 3% of simulations. Closing it takes about 114,981 voters switching sides, or 229,962 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +22.4 and R +5.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Jefferson, a projected net 113,889 votes; Fayette, a projected net 43,833 votes; Franklin, a projected net 3,834 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Kenton, R +10.0, 3.7% of the vote; Warren, R +11.5, 2.7% of the vote; Campbell, R +7.0, 2.2% of the vote; Hardin, R +11.5, 2.2% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Charles Booker runs furthest behind in Boone, Laurel, Oldham. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 90% of voters, 40 to 60, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.52 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 69% of voters, 43 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.44 points; Voters without a degree, 67% of voters, 41 to 59, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.36 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Charles Booker: Immigration voters 13 to 87, Small counties 32 to 68, Voters who can afford daily costs 36 to 64. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$310K cash against $2.3M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
